sources.title: September Pixel Drop: New Pixel VIP updates, Pixel Watch features, and more
Google Pixel Watch Update (Pixel Watch 5) - September 2026
Protect yourself with spam & scam detection on your Pixel phone

verified_facts.fact: Google published the September 2026 Pixel Drop announcement on its own blog on 2026-09-15. The page's JSON-LD gives datePublished 2026-09-15T18:00:00+00:00 and dateModified 2026-09-15T18:20:54.745901+00:00; the meta tag article:published_time is 2026-09-15; the visible date line reads 'Sep 15, 2026'.

The official headline of the blog post is 'September Pixel Drop: New Pixel VIP updates, Pixel Watch features, and more'. The browser-tab/og title is shorter: 'September Pixel Drop: VIP updates, Pixel Watch features'.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: September Pixel Drop: New Pixel VIP updates, Pixel Watch features, and more

verified_facts.fact: Google's own one-line description of the post is: 'Our September Pixel Drop is here with an updated Pixel VIP widget, expanded chat Scam Detection, and more.'
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: Our September Pixel Drop is here with an updated Pixel VIP widget, expanded chat Scam Detection, and more.

verified_facts.fact: The blog post carries no author byline (unlike other blog.google posts such as the Pause Point one, which names an author). It is published under Google, not a named person.

The blog post is four short paragraphs plus a pointer sentence; the whole body is about 160 words. Its last line is 'Visit our community forum post to learn more.', linking to support.google.com/pixelphone/thread/466181739 - i.e. Google itself designates that forum thread as its own detailed release note ('our community forum post').
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: Visit our community forum post to learn more.

verified_facts.fact: Blog wording for the phone features: 'Stay connected to your VIPs with updated home screen widgets that let you call or text people with a single tap, or switch between contacts using the bottom floating overlay navigation menu. New notification badges ensure you never miss a message. And Pixel now makes it easier to avoid scams with inline Gboard warnings in the U.S. and expanded Scam Detection for chat app notifications in more regions.'
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: Stay connected to your VIPs with updated home screen widgets that let you call or text people with a single tap, or switch between contacts using the bottom floating overlay navigation menu. New notification badges ensure you never miss a message. And Pixel now makes it easier to avoid scams with inline Gboard warnings in the U.S. and expanded Scam Detection for chat app notifications in more regions.

verified_facts.fact: Blog wording for the watch features: 'If you have a Pixel Watch, you'll receive Raise to Talk improvements, and additional One Handed gesture app integrations, along with other bug fixes.' The blog does NOT name a watch model here; the linked support thread does (Pixel Watch 5 only).
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: If you have a Pixel Watch, you’ll receive Raise to Talk improvements, and additional One Handed gesture app integrations, along with other bug fixes.

verified_facts.fact: Blog wording for the Harry Potter tie-in: 'Instantly customize your Pixel with Harry Potter Audiobook Packs to celebrate the release of Harry Potter: The Full-Cast Audio Editions on Audible. To begin your journey to Hogwarts, all eligible Pixel users will receive a two-month Audible free trial.' The blog states no countries and no end date for this offer; the support thread does.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: To begin your journey to Hogwarts, all eligible Pixel users will receive a two-month Audible free trial.

verified_facts.fact: The blog's hero image alt text is: 'Text "Pixel Drop" surrounded by the Google G and several glossy, pink, puffy 3D cloud-like shapes'. (Recorded only so the writer knows Google's own art is branded; our own artwork must not reproduce it.)
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: Text “Pixel Drop” surrounded by the Google G and several glossy, pink, puffy 3D cloud-like shapes

verified_facts.fact: Google's forum release note is titled 'September 2026 Pixel Drop' and defines a Pixel Drop as: 'Your Pixel devices become even more helpful with Pixel Drops. They're automatic software updates that send new and upgraded features to your phone.'
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: Your Pixel devices become even more helpful with Pixel Drops. They’re automatic software updates that send new and upgraded features to your phone.

verified_facts.fact: Rollout timing, verbatim: 'Supported Pixel devices will receive these software updates starting today. The rollout of these features will continue over the coming weeks in phases, depending on carrier and device.' Google gives no completion date and names no carriers.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: Supported Pixel devices will receive these software updates starting today. The rollout of these features will continue over the coming weeks in phases, depending on carrier and device.

verified_facts.fact: Google tells users they will be notified when the update is available and points them to 'Update to the latest Android version' and 'update your apps' - i.e. some of these features arrive via app updates, not only the system update.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: You will receive a notification once the system update is available for your device.

verified_facts.fact: Google frames the list as partial: 'Here are just some of the features to look forward to in the September Pixel Drop:' - so the five named features are explicitly not the complete list.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: Here are just some of the features to look forward to in the September Pixel Drop:

verified_facts.fact: Feature 1, Pixel VIPs updates, verbatim: 'Stay seamlessly connected to your VIP contacts. With newly designed, expanded widget options, you can use quick actions to send a call or text to your VIP contacts with a single tap straight from your home screen. New, glanceable notification badges ensure you never miss an urgent or unread message, and you can also switch effortlessly between VIPs using the bottom floating menu.' No region, language or carrier condition is attached to this feature anywhere in the note.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: With newly designed, expanded widget options, you can use quick actions to send a call or text to your VIP contacts with a single tap straight from your home screen.

verified_facts.fact: Feature 2, Harry Potter Audiobook Packs, verbatim: 'One tap changes your wallpaper, icons, and sounds with elements from the audiobooks - no wand required.' It is a theme pack (wallpaper + icons + sounds), tied to the release of 'Harry Potter: The Full-Cast Audio Editions' on Audible.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: One tap changes your wallpaper, icons, and sounds with elements from the audiobooks - no wand required.

verified_facts.fact: Feature 3a, Scam Detection in the keyboard: 'Starting in the U.S. on Pixel 6 and newer phones, Scam Detection is arriving directly on your Gboard across your favorite messaging apps. When you start typing a response to a suspicious message, a "Likely scam" warning chip will appear right above your keys. Processing happens in real-time and on your device, keeping your conversations private to you.' Two conditions are stated in one sentence: United States only, AND Pixel 6 or newer.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: Starting in the U.S. on Pixel 6 and newer phones, Scam Detection is arriving directly on your Gboard across your favorite messaging apps.

verified_facts.fact: The on-device / real-time processing claim for keyboard Scam Detection is Google's own statement, not something this site tested: 'Processing happens in real-time and on your device, keeping your conversations private to you'.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: Processing happens in real-time and on your device, keeping your conversations private to you

verified_facts.fact: Footnote 3, attached to the word 'Gboard', says the keyboard warning is not Gboard-exclusive: 'Available on other keyboards with Keyboard Suggestions.'
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: Available on other keyboards with Keyboard Suggestions.

verified_facts.fact: Footnote 4, attached to the keyboard Scam Detection paragraph, narrows it further: 'Available only in select languages in the US.' Google does not name which languages.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: Available only in select languages in the US.

verified_facts.fact: Feature 3b, Scam Detection in chat notifications, verbatim: 'Already available in the US for Pixel 6+ devices, we're now expanding this feature to nine new countries (Australia, Canada, France, Germany, India, Japan, Mexico, Singapore, and the United Kingdom) and six new languages (Arabic, French, German, Portuguese, Japanese, and Spanish), helping protect even more people worldwide.' That is exactly nine countries and six languages, listed by name. Taiwan is not among them.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: we’re now expanding this feature to nine new countries (Australia, Canada, France, Germany, India, Japan, Mexico, Singapore, and the United Kingdom) and six new languages (Arabic, French, German, Portuguese, Japanese, and Spanish)

verified_facts.fact: Google describes the notification-level Scam Detection as pre-existing, not new in this Drop: it 'automatically flags suspicious incoming chat notifications with a “Likely scam” warning chip before you even open them', and the note links back to Google's own November 2025 Pixel Drop post as its origin. What is new in September 2026 is the country/language expansion plus the keyboard placement.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: This adds another layer of defense alongside Scam Detection in notifications

verified_facts.fact: Feature 4, Pause Point, verbatim: 'Pause Point helps you cut down on unintentional app use. It adds a pause before you open a distracting app of your choice, giving you a moment to decide whether you really want to continue. First introduced on Pixel 11, Pause Point is now rolling out to Pixel 6 and newer devices as part of this update.' Pause Point is in the forum release note and in the device table but is NOT mentioned in the blog post at all.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: First introduced on Pixel 11, Pause Point is now rolling out to Pixel 6 and newer devices as part of this update.

verified_facts.fact: The forum note contains a section headed 'Feature Availability by Device' carrying footnote 5. The matrix itself is a PNG image attachment inside that thread (storage.googleapis.com/support-forums-api/attachment/thread-466181739-2189480914184742135.png, 1743x629, filename 'Screenshot 2026-09-15 11.54.42 PM.png'), not HTML text - so it is invisible to text-only scraping and to screen readers, and there is no text alternative in the thread.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: Feature Availability by Device

verified_facts.fact: The device matrix has 25 device columns, in this order: Pixel 11 Pro Fold, Pixel 11 Pro XL, Pixel 11 Pro, Pixel 11, Pixel 10 Pro Fold, Pixel 10 Pro XL, Pixel 10 Pro, Pixel 10, Pixel 10a, Pixel 9 Pro Fold, Pixel 9 Pro XL, Pixel 9 Pro, Pixel 9, Pixel 9a, Pixel 8 Pro, Pixel 8, Pixel 8a, Pixel Fold, Pixel 7 Pro, Pixel 7, Pixel 7a, Pixel 6 Pro, Pixel 6, Pixel 6a, Pixel Tablet. That is 24 phones plus Pixel Tablet. No Pixel 5a or older model appears in the table at all.

The device matrix has exactly five feature rows: 'Pixel VIPs updates'; 'Harry Potter Audiobook Packs'; 'Scam Detection in chat message notifications market expansion (AU, CA, DE, FR, IN, JP, MX, SG, and UK) and language expansion (AR, DE, ES, FR, DE, PT, and JA)'; 'Scam Detection in keyboard launch in the US'; 'Pause Point'.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: Scam Detection in chat message notifications market expansion (AU, CA, DE, FR, IN, JP, MX, SG, and UK) and language expansion (AR, DE, ES, FR, DE, PT, and JA)

verified_facts.fact: In the device matrix, all 24 phone columns (Pixel 6 / 6a through Pixel 11 Pro Fold) carry a tick for every one of the five features. Pixel Tablet is listed as a column but carries NO tick for any of the five features - checked cell by cell at 3x magnification. So Google's own table says the Pixel Tablet gets none of the five named features.

Footnote 5, attached to the device table, is the only availability caveat Google attaches to the VIP widget and Harry Potter rows: 'Feature availability may vary by country and/or language.' It names no country.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: Feature availability may vary by country and/or language.

verified_facts.fact: The language-expansion label inside the device-matrix image reads '(AR, DE, ES, FR, DE, PT, and JA)' - seven codes for six languages, with DE appearing twice. The prose in the same note lists six: Arabic, French, German, Portuguese, Japanese, and Spanish. The duplication is Google's own; it is a defect in the source image, not a transcription error on our side.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: language expansion (AR, DE, ES, FR, DE, PT, and JA)

verified_facts.fact: Disclaimer 1, on eligibility in general: 'Pixel Drops are provided during applicable Android update and support periods for your device. See g.co/pixel/updates for details. Feature availability varies by model. Devices sold separately.'
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: Pixel Drops are provided during applicable Android update and support periods for your device. See g.co/pixel/updates for details. Feature availability varies by model. Devices sold separately.

verified_facts.fact: Disclaimer 2 gives the only two hard dates in the whole Drop: 'Harry Potter Audiobook Packs available until December 31, 2026. Audible offer available until January 14, 2027 only in the United States, Canada, United Kingdom, France, Germany, Italy, Spain, India, Japan, and Australia.' That is ten named countries; Taiwan is not among them. Note the theme packs (31 Dec 2026) and the Audible trial (14 Jan 2027) expire on different dates.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: Harry Potter Audiobook Packs available until December 31, 2026. Audible offer available until January 14, 2027 only in the United States, Canada, United Kingdom, France, Germany, Italy, Spain, India, Japan, and Australia.

verified_facts.fact: The ten Audible-offer countries are not the same set as the ten Scam Detection countries. The Audible list adds Italy and Spain and omits Mexico and Singapore; the Scam Detection list adds Mexico and Singapore and omits Italy and Spain. Both lists are in the same forum note.
The Pixel Watch thread Google links from the blog post is titled 'Google Pixel Watch Update (Pixel Watch 5) - September 2026' - the model restriction is in the title itself.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: Google Pixel Watch Update (Pixel Watch 5) - September 2026

verified_facts.fact: The watch update is a Wear OS 7 update and is limited to one model: 'All eligible Pixel Watch 5 devices will receive a Wear OS 7 update. The rollout will continue over the coming weeks in phases depending on carrier and device.' A separate 'Device Applicability' section repeats it: 'Applicable updates are available for the following models: Pixel Watch 5'.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: All eligible Pixel Watch 5 devices will receive a Wear OS 7 update.

verified_facts.fact: The watch build number is given under a heading 'Software version' / 'Global': 'Pixel Watch 5: CP3A.260905.002'. It is listed as Global, with no per-region build.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: Pixel Watch 5: CP3A.260905.002

verified_facts.fact: Watch feature - Gemini Personalization: 'Personalization makes Gemini on Watch more helpful by learning from past conversations and connected Google apps (Gmail, Calendar, Search, YouTube, Photos) to deliver personalized responses. Users can ask queries like "What's on my calendar today?" or "Find the tracking number in my email" and receive answers tailored to their data. The feature is powered by an offline user profile and real-time online retrieval working together.' Five connected apps are named. No region or language condition is stated for it.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: learning from past conversations and connected Google apps (Gmail, Calendar, Search, YouTube, Photos) to deliver personalized responses

verified_facts.fact: Watch feature - Proactive suggestions, described as: 'Gemini Intelligence Proactive Suggestions turns complex, multi-step tasks into seamless one-tap actions in messages. If a loved one asks when is the dinner with family, Gemini automatically locates the info in your calendar and surfaces it directly on your wrist'. It carries footnote 1, the tightest condition in the entire Drop: 'Available only on Pixel Watch 5 paired with Pixel 11. Also requires gemini and proactive assistance enabled on paired Pixel 11.'
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: Available only on Pixel Watch 5 paired with Pixel 11. Also requires gemini and proactive assistance enabled on paired Pixel 11.

verified_facts.fact: Watch feature - Offline Gemini: 'Powered by on-device AI, Gemini can process core actions instantly with low latency, even when you're completely offline. Examples are setting up a timer, starting/stopping a workout, turning on do not disturb and other device actions.' Four example actions are named; 'low latency' is Google's claim, not a measurement.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: Powered by on-device AI, Gemini can process core actions instantly with low latency, even when you’re completely offline.

verified_facts.fact: Watch feature - Raise to talk improvements, in full: 'Updates and improvements for raise to talk gesture model.' That single sentence is everything Google says about it; the blog post capitalises it as 'Raise to Talk' while the support thread writes 'raise to talk'.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: Updates and improvements for raise to talk gesture model.

verified_facts.fact: Watch feature - GPS: Google's heading is 'Our most accurate GPS route tracking' and the body is 'Major improvements to the route maps displayed on Google Health app after running, biking, hiking, and walking sessions.' 'Most accurate' is a vendor superlative with no figure attached and no comparison baseline.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: Our most accurate GPS route tracking

verified_facts.fact: Watch feature - the gesture work the blog calls 'One Handed gesture app integrations' is headed 'Hand Gestures App Expansions' in Google's own support thread, and lists eight items: double pinch to open At a Glance from watch face; double pinch to open notification center from watch face; double pinch to scroll through Gemini response; double pinch to scroll through cards in Wallet app; double pinch to scroll through your workout metrics; double pinch to toggle between Google Maps views; double pinch to manage Recorder app; wrist turn gesture as universal back navigation.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: Hand Gestures App Expansions

verified_facts.fact: The watch note ends its feature list with 'General bug fixes and improvements', is signed 'Thanks, Google Pixel Watch Support Team', and points to the Pixel Watch Security Bulletin at source.android.com/docs/security/bulletin/pixel-watch for 'applicable security fixes'.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: Details regarding applicable security fixes can be found on the Pixel Watch Security Bulletin

verified_facts.fact: The same watch thread lists Google's previous Pixel Watch updates of 2026 as 'June (Pixel Watch 2, 3, & 4)', 'March EMR (Pixel Watch 1)' and 'March (Pixel Watch 2, 3, & 4)'. That is the only official indication in the thread of what older watch models have received; it does not say whether Watch 1-4 get anything in September 2026.

Google's Help Centre page 'Protect yourself with spam & scam detection on your Pixel phone' lists the CUMULATIVE state of Scam Detection after this Drop: 'Scam Detection is available in these regions: Australia, Canada, France, Germany, India, Japan, Mexico, Singapore, Spain, United Kingdom, United States.' That is eleven regions. Taiwan is not listed.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: Scam Detection is available in these regions:

verified_facts.fact: The same Help Centre page lists eight languages: Arabic, English, French, German, Indonesian, Japanese, Portuguese, Spanish. Chinese in any form is not listed.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: Scam Detection is available in the following languages:

verified_facts.fact: The Help Centre region list (11) does not match the Drop announcement arithmetic (US already supported + nine new = 10). The Help Centre additionally lists Spain, and additionally lists English and Indonesian among the languages, neither of which appears in the Drop's 'six new languages'. Google does not reconcile the two lists anywhere I could reach. Treat the Help Centre page as the current cumulative state and the forum note as the September delta, and say so.

The Help Centre confirms the US-only scope of the keyboard variant independently of the Drop note: 'This feature helps detect likely scams by analyzing new message notifications from supported apps. For users in the US, this feature can also help detect scams when using the keyboard in select apps.'
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: For users in the US, this feature can also help detect scams when using the keyboard in select apps.

verified_facts.fact: Help Centre on where the warning appears: 'Possible scam message notifications have a red warning icon and display a “Likely scam” button when expanded. For users in the US, the warning button may also show under the suspicious message in the notification panel, in the keyboard, or both.'
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: For users in the US, the warning button may also show under the suspicious message in the notification panel, in the keyboard, or both.

verified_facts.fact: Help Centre on the setting: 'Scam Detection for chat messages is on by default.' The path is Settings app > Security & privacy > More security & privacy > Scam Detection > turn 'Message scams' on or off. In Google's own Traditional-Chinese rendering of the same page these read 設定 > 安全性與隱私權 > 其他安全性和隱私權設定 > 詐騙偵測 > 訊息詐騙, the feature is 詐騙偵測 and the warning chip is 疑似詐騙.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: Scam Detection for chat messages is on by default.

verified_facts.fact: Help Centre on data handling: 'This feature runs in a secure, isolated environment to identify suspicious patterns... Your message content remains private and isn't sent to Google, unless you choose to share it.' If a user taps to share a flagged message, 'Only the selected message content will be shared, without common identifying info.'
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: Your message content remains private and isn’t sent to Google, unless you choose to share it.

verified_facts.fact: Google states the limit of the feature itself: 'Important: Scam Detection may not catch every scam. Be careful when you share personal info or tap on links.' Also: 'If you mark a message as “Not a scam,” Scam Detection is turned off for that conversation for a while.'
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: Important: Scam Detection may not catch every scam. Be careful when you share personal info or tap on links.

not_said: Taiwan. Taiwan is named nowhere in any of the four sources. It is not in the nine new Scam Detection countries, not in the eleven Help Centre regions, and not in the ten Audible-offer countries. Traditional or Simplified Chinese is not in the eight supported Scam Detection languages. Google does not say Taiwan is excluded either - it simply does not appear. Write this as '官方未提及台灣', never as '台灣不能用' for the features Google gave no region list for.

No price. Nothing in the Drop is priced. The Audible trial is described only as 'a two-month Audible free trial' with no statement of what it costs after the trial and no statement of whether a payment method is required.

'All eligible Pixel users' for the Audible trial is never defined. Google does not say what makes a user eligible beyond the ten listed countries, does not say whether existing or lapsed Audible subscribers qualify, and does not say how the trial is claimed.

No rollout completion date. 'Over the coming weeks in phases, depending on carrier and device' is the only schedule, for both the phone Drop and the Pixel Watch 5 Wear OS 7 update. No carrier is named and no phase order is given.
No Android version number and no phone build number. The Pixel Watch thread gives a build (CP3A.260905.002) but the phone thread gives none, and names no Android release. Do not supply one.

No region condition at all is stated for Pixel VIPs updates, for Harry Potter Audiobook Packs (beyond the ten-country Audible trial), or for Pause Point. The only thing covering them is the blanket footnote 'Feature availability may vary by country and/or language.' So Google neither promises nor denies these three in Taiwan.
No region or language condition is stated for any Pixel Watch feature, including Gemini Personalization. The build is labelled 'Global' and that is all.

The blog post does not say Pixel Watch features are Pixel Watch 5 only - it just says 'If you have a Pixel Watch'. Only the linked support thread restricts it. Do not repeat the blog's looser wording without the restriction.
The blog post does not mention Pause Point, Gemini Personalization, Proactive suggestions, Offline Gemini or the GPS route-tracking change at all. Those exist only in the support threads.

Pixel Tablet's blank row is a blank row, not a sentence. Google's table shows no tick for Pixel Tablet on any of the five features, but Google never writes 'Pixel Tablet does not get these'. Report it as 'Google's table marks none of the five features for Pixel Tablet'.
Google never says which languages the US keyboard Scam Detection covers. Footnote 4 only says 'Available only in select languages in the US.'

There is no stated relationship between this Pixel Drop and Android's own September 2026 Drop. blog.google's related-stories rail shows a separate 'September Android Drop' post; the Pixel Drop note does not reference it.
Google does not say whether Pixel Watch 1 through 4 receive anything in September 2026. The thread only lists their previous updates (June, and March EMR for Watch 1).

No measured performance figures anywhere. 'Our most accurate GPS route tracking', 'low latency', 'real-time', 'processing happens on your device' are Google's characterisations with no numbers and no methodology.

As of 2026-09-16 there is no September 2026 Pixel Watch security bulletin published: source.android.com/docs/security/bulletin/pixel-watch lists August 2026 (published August 20, 2026, patch level 2026-08-05) as the newest entry and the page footer reads 'Last updated 2026-08-20 UTC', even though the watch release note points readers there for 'applicable security fixes'. Do not name a September patch level.

Google published no Traditional-Chinese version of this Pixel Drop post: blog.google/intl/zh-tw/products-and-platforms/devices/pixel/september-2026-pixel-drop/ returns HTTP 404 (while blog.google/intl/zh-tw/ returns 200). Taiwanese readers only have the English post plus the machine-assisted Chinese Help Centre page.

unverified_or_excluded.claim: Exact posting dates and times of the two Google support-forum threads.
unverified_or_excluded.seen_where: Decoded internal timestamp arrays inside the threads' inline JSON: the phone thread carries 1789496860754770 microseconds = 2026-09-15T18:27:40Z (27 minutes after the blog post), the watch thread carries 1788292062825882 = 2026-09-01T19:47:42Z with a later value 1788456498201866 = 2026-09-03T17:28:18Z.
unverified_or_excluded.why_excluded: These are undocumented internal fields, not a displayed publication date, and the threads render no visible date, no JSON-LD and no og: date to curl. The phone thread's value lines up plausibly with the blog post, the watch thread's does not (it would predate the Drop by two weeks). I will not state either as fact. Practical consequence for the writer: do NOT write that the Pixel Watch 5 Wear OS 7 update 'was announced on 15 September' - write that Google's Pixel Drop post links to a Pixel Watch 5 update note, and date only the blog post.

unverified_or_excluded.claim: That the forum threads are written by Google staff.
unverified_or_excluded.seen_where: The phone thread's byline is 'Kush M.' and the watch thread's is 'Stefanie Frederick'; the pages contain badge label strings ('Community Manager', 'Product Expert', 'Google Employee') but only in the UI string dictionary, so I could not tie a badge to either author from this container.
unverified_or_excluded.why_excluded: Google Support Community threads can also be posted by volunteer Product Experts, who are not Google. I treat these two as first-party on different grounds: the blog post calls the phone thread 'our community forum post' and links it, and the watch thread is signed 'Google Pixel Watch Support Team'. Attribute to 'Google' / 'Google 的說明論壇公告', never to the personal names.

unverified_or_excluded.claim: The Audible offer's terms (two-month length, price after trial, sign-up mechanics).

editorial_brief:
RECOMMENDATION FIRST: write this as a STANDALONE tech article, not as a secondary item. The candidates file graded it '份量偏輕，建議放次要新聞' on the strength of the 160-word blog post alone. That grading is now out of date: Google's own forum release note, which the blog post itself calls 'our community forum post', carries a 25-column device matrix, two hard expiry dates, a ten-country offer list, a nine-country plus six-language expansion list, a fifth feature the blog never mentions (Pause Point), and a Pixel Watch note that narrows the whole watch story to one model paired with one phone. That is more verified, conditional, reader-checkable detail than several items already ranked as important news. There is easily enough for 1,800-3,000 characters without padding. Final call is the site owner's; if it stays secondary, the device/region table is the part to keep.

READER: a Taiwanese Pixel owner - Pixel 6 through Pixel 11, possibly a Pixel Watch - who saw a headline saying 'Google adds scam warnings to the keyboard' and wants to know whether anything in it reaches their phone.

ANGLE (this is the article's reason to exist): a Feature Drop is not one thing. Its five features are gated in three different ways, and Google states each gate in a different place. (a) Device gate: the matrix ticks 24 phone models, Pixel 6/6a up to Pixel 11 Pro Fold, for all five features, and ticks Pixel Tablet for none. (b) Region and language gate: keyboard Scam Detection is United States only and 'select languages in the US'; notification Scam Detection adds nine named countries and six named languages; the Audible trial covers ten named countries until 14 January 2027; the theme packs themselves expire 31 December 2026. (c) Pairing gate: the watch's Proactive suggestions need a Pixel Watch 5 paired with a Pixel 11 with Gemini and proactive assistance turned on. Taiwan appears in none of the lists - which for a Taiwanese reader sorts the Drop cleanly into 'the VIP widget changes and Pause Point, subject to Google's blanket may-vary footnote' versus 'the scam-warning headline, which is a US and nine-other-countries story'. Say that plainly and let the reader check their own model; do not turn it into a complaint about Google or a prediction of when Taiwan gets it.

SECOND ANGLE worth two paragraphs: where the real release note lives. The blog post says 'If you have a Pixel Watch' - the note it links says Pixel Watch 5 only. The blog post names three phone features - the note names five. The blog gives no dates - the note gives two. And the device matrix that answers 'does my phone get this' is a PNG screenshot inside a forum thread, with no text alternative. That is a concrete, non-preachy point about how to read any vendor Feature Drop, and it is the kind of thing this site can say because it actually opened both pages.

STRUCTURE FIT: five H2 sections come naturally - (1) what was announced on 15 September and where the real note is; (2) the five phone features and the device matrix, with the required table at the end of section 2; (3) the region and language lists, with the diagram at the end of section 3; (4) the Pixel Watch 5 side and its pairing condition; (5) what Google does not say, including Taiwan, dates, build numbers and the Pixel Tablet row. TABLE (max 4 columns, short cells, caption with 查核日 2026-09-16): suggested columns 功能 / 適用機型 / 地區與語言條件 / 官方期限, rows Pixel VIPs 小工具, Harry Potter 套件, 鍵盤詐騙警示, 通知詐騙警示, Pause Point. DIAGRAM 2x2: 機型關卡 / 地區關卡 / 語言關卡 / 配對關卡 - every number drawn on it must also appear in the body text.

LIVED-EXPERIENCE EXAMPLES must be labelled as editor-designed, per BRIEF.md. A safe one: a reader checks Settings > 安全性與隱私權 > 其他安全性和隱私權設定 > 詐騙偵測 and finds 訊息詐騙 already on by default - that path is sourced from Google's own Chinese Help Centre page, but flag that Google marks that page as machine-assisted translation.

SUMMARY block: first sentence is the answer - Google shipped the September Pixel Drop on 15 September 2026 with five features across 24 Pixel phone models. Then the conditions: keyboard scam warnings are US-only; notification scam warnings add nine countries and six languages; the watch update is Pixel Watch 5 only. Last sentence is the caveat: Taiwan is not named in any of Google's lists and Google attaches 'availability may vary by country and/or language' to the rest. Every number in the summary must already be in the body verbatim.

FAQ candidates that these sources genuinely answer: 我的 Pixel 有沒有在名單上（列到 Pixel 6/6a）; 台灣拿得到鍵盤的詐騙警示嗎（官方名單沒有台灣，官方也沒說台灣不能用）; Pixel 平板呢（官方表格五項都沒有打勾）; 哈利波特套件到什麼時候（套件到 2026-12-31、Audible 試用到 2027-01-14 且限十國）; 哪一款手錶會更新（只有 Pixel Watch 5，版本 CP3A.260905.002）; 什麼時候會更新到我手上（官方只說 starting today 之後分批數週，依電信業者與機型而定）.
must_not_write: No buying or upgrade advice of any kind - tech.md bars 該不該買 / 值不值得升級 / 哪一支比較好. Listing which model gets which feature is allowed; concluding which model to get is not.
Do not write that Taiwan is excluded, blocked or unsupported. Google names Taiwan nowhere. Write 官方公告未提及台灣 and, for the features with no region list, 官方只說可用性可能因國家或語言而異.

Do not restate Google's capability claims as fact. 'Most accurate GPS route tracking', 'low latency', 'real-time', 'processing happens on your device', 'keeping your conversations private' are all Google 表示. This site ran no test - never write 我們實測.

Do not invent an Android version, a phone build number, a September 2026 Pixel Watch security patch level, a Taiwan launch date or a rollout completion date. None exists in any source; the only build published is the watch's CP3A.260905.002.

Do not silently fix Google's duplicated 'DE' in the image's language list (AR, DE, ES, FR, DE, PT, and JA). Use the six-language prose list for the body and, if the discrepancy is mentioned, attribute it to the source table.
Do not merge the ten Audible countries with the nine Scam Detection countries - they are different sets (Audible adds Italy and Spain, omits Mexico and Singapore).
Do not carry the blog's loose phrasing 'If you have a Pixel Watch' without Google's own restriction to Pixel Watch 5.
Do not attribute anything to the forum posters' personal names ('Kush M.', 'Stefanie Frederick'). Attribute to Google.
Do not describe or evaluate Pixel 11 / Pixel Watch 5 hardware. The sources only use those names.
No finance disclaimer callout - tech.md says the tech vertical must not carry one.
No trademark, wordmark, logo, mascot or UI screenshot in the hero or the SVG diagram; write product names as plain text.
Do not write anything about how scams are actually carried out. Batch 3's threat-report rule applies: scope and what the user should do, never attack technique.
No list formatting, no Markdown, no emoji, no Simplified Chinese characters in the zh-TW pack.

corrections_to_candidate_list: docs/news-2026-batch-4/candidates-tech-and-ai.md line ~261 says '官方沒說：除了美國以外哪些地區拿得到哪些功能、適用哪些 Pixel 機型、分批時程'. The first two thirds of that are wrong. Google DOES state which regions: nine named new countries (Australia, Canada, France, Germany, India, Japan, Mexico, Singapore, United Kingdom) and six named new languages for notification Scam Detection, plus eleven cumulative regions and eight languages on the Help Centre page, plus ten named countries for the Audible offer. Google ALSO states which Pixel models: a 25-column matrix covering Pixel 6/6a through Pixel 11 Pro Fold plus Pixel Tablet. Only '分批時程' is genuinely unstated. The detail was not missing, it was one click below the blog post in the forum note Google links.

The same entry lists the features as if the blog post were the full release note. It omits Pause Point, which is the fifth feature in Google's own note and the fifth row of the device matrix, and it omits the two expiry dates (packs until 2026-12-31, Audible offer until 2027-01-14).

The entry's Pixel Watch line - 'Pixel Watch 有 Raise to Talk 改進、One Handed 手勢支援更多 App、錯誤修正' - reproduces the blog's loose wording. Google's linked note is titled 'Google Pixel Watch Update (Pixel Watch 5) - September 2026', restricts the update to Pixel Watch 5, gives build CP3A.260905.002, calls the gesture work 'Hand Gestures App Expansions' (eight gestures, not 'One Handed'), and adds four features the blog never names (Gemini Personalization, Proactive suggestions, Offline Gemini, GPS route tracking) plus a pairing condition (Pixel Watch 5 + Pixel 11).
The recommendation at lines ~262 and ~344 ('份量偏輕，我仍建議當次要新聞') should be revisited. On the full first-party material this is comfortably a standalone article; it was graded on the blog post alone.

The feed table at the top of the candidates file is accurate for blog.google (RSS 200) but should gain a warning for support.google.com: those threads return HTTP 200 and ~2 MB, yet naive tag-stripping yields under 1 KB of navigation chrome because the post body sits in a double-escaped JSON blob inside an inline script. This is a third variant of the file's own '200 does not mean you got the document' trap and will silently defeat the next agent that tries to read a Google support thread.
standalone_or_secondary: STANDALONE recommended. Substance actually available from first-party sources: 5 phone features, a 25-column x 5-row device matrix, 9 expansion countries, 6 expansion languages, 11 cumulative regions, 8 cumulative languages, 10 Audible countries, 2 expiry dates, 1 watch build number, 8 watch gestures, 4 additional watch features and 2 pairing conditions.
